bull.b: Sustained revenue expansion alongside high branded gross margins indicates strong product economics and growing commercial traction. This combination can support reinvestment in sales and development, improve operating leverage, and strengthen Harrow’s competitive position over the next several quarters.

The leading products are contributing substantial revenue growth across multiple ophthalmic categories rather than relying on one product alone. Continued adoption of VEVYE, IHEEZO and TRIESENCE could broaden the revenue base and create a more durable commercial platform.

TYRVAYA expands Harrow’s dry-eye offering with an already approved product, established distribution and an experienced sales team. Integrating it with VEVYE and existing infrastructure may increase provider reach, cross-selling opportunities and the scale of the ocular-surface franchise.

bear.b: Rapidly rising debt combined with shrinking equity leaves Harrow with limited balance-sheet flexibility and a debt-to-equity level near 10 times. This can constrain investment choices, increase financing pressure, and make execution more sensitive to any operating shortfall.

bear.t: Weak recent cash generation and profitability
bear.b: The latest reversal into negative operating and free cash flow shows that recent growth has not yet translated consistently into internally funded expansion. Combined with renewed net losses, this may require greater reliance on financing and limit the company’s ability to absorb execution challenges.

bear.t: Lower earnings outlook and licensing uncertainty
bear.b: The sharply reduced EBITDA outlook signals weaker near-term earnings conversion because of lower margins, development spending and TYRVAYA transition costs. The separate VEVYE licensing matter adds contractual uncertainty that could complicate the economics or integration of the expanded portfolio.
